body: I wasn't able to make this happen. Are you sure that `$articles` is an instance of `Entity` and not something else?
I was also not able to reproduce this problem by accessing undefined properties on a Collection/Query object either. What is `bla bytes` in your example?

It was definitely an ''Entity'' object, but I'm off the computer now to reply about the memory. I doubt that's the culprit though. There was also a 10 second delay before which signifies an endless loop
(there should have been a Question mark at the end of the previous message, damn touchscreens)
What does your entity class look like?
Can you show the full code that triggers the memory error? I'm interested in seeing the find operation and also knowing how many rows your are selecting.
Is that your actual code? what is `$something`?

It's an example of how it fails. I don't want it to actually _do_ something at this point with this code, I was just fooling around with 3.0 and hit on it accidentally. I believe a missing object property shouldn't cause a fatal error that's why I reported it.
Please don't give us partial examples, It would be more helpful to paste the real example to see if there is anything wrong that you may be missing.
I do appreciate your time and I'm sorry if I'm wasting it with something trivial (hopefully not). This minimal code I've pasted above is exactly the one that causes the error.

If that is the example, then I would check if the variable `$something` is defined before using it, doing that in a look is going to create plenty errors and consume memory. I will check if using an empty value for accessing stuff in the entity triggers any other special problem
Thank you (both) for your time once again.
